html:
SMTO-GIT-0008 — The Git project address has a sign-in name or isn't valid

GUID: e4eabc05-1f05-453e-8a2d-1768a7532dc7
Slug: git-public-url-invalid
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • The address saved for a Git project contains a user name or password, or isn't a valid address. SMTO keeps sign-in details only in their own private fields, so it didn't accept this address.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the parameter that holds this Git project's address, open its Value tab, and select Reveal & edit value. The address and its sign-in fields are all kept in that one parameter, and it must be revealed before you can change it.
  2. In url, delete anything between :// and the @ sign. For example, change https://name:token@github.com/team/project.git to https://github.com/team/project.git. SMTO won't save a password or token inside the address, because the address can be shown in plain text.
  3. For an SSH address like ssh://git@github.com/team/project.git, write it as git@github.com:team/project.git instead. The short SSH form doesn't count as a sign-in name inside the address, so SMTO accepts it.
  4. Put the user name in username and the password or access token in token, then select Save. Those fields are kept private and are used when SMTO connects to the project.

What success looks like

  • Save completes without this message, and the url field shows the address with no name or password in it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your token into the address or into the conversation; keep it only in the token field.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The git_repository profile URL contains embedded userinfo or fails URL parsing, or a saved Git remote URL failed the safe-remote check (length, control characters or scheme).

What this means

  • Git profile URL parsing rejects embedded userinfo or malformed URL syntax, or saved remote URL inventory fails its supported safe shape. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • Git profile URL parsing rejects embedded userinfo or malformed URL syntax, or saved remote URL inventory fails its supported safe shape.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish a profile URL problem from a malformed saved remote list; inspect syntax without disclosing credentials.

How to fix it

  • For a Parameter Store git_repository profile, remove userinfo from url (any '://' URL with a username, including ssh://git@host) and move credentials into username and token; use scp-style git@host:path for SSH. If the failure came from a saved conversation working-context record instead, its remote URL failed gateway_core.git_context.safe_remote (at most 384 characters, no control characters, scheme http, https, ssh, git or file); rerun a Git command in the repository root so a fresh record replaces it.
  • Correct the repository URL and store authentication in the supported username/token fields. Rediscover the repository without exposing credentials.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Rediscovered remote URLs validate and authentication stays in supported private fields.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
